transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jia Li (CSM), Ravi Mehta (SE) - Elmwood: Carlos Mendoza (Head of ML), Priya Singh (Platform Eng), Leah Thompson (CFO)

Summary (auto-gen):
Quarterly business review focused on usage trends (embeddings + chat), rising token costs, latency incidents in Feb, and roadmap alignment for Dedicated/private deployment later this year. Agreed to run a technical benchmark and share compliance docs.

Topics: usage and cost, reliability incidents, Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, roadmap & timelines, security/compliance asks.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, can we do quick intros?
[00:06] Carlos: yeah, Carlos here, head of ml at Elmwood, we run the customer support agent and internal search embeddings, thanks for having us.
[00:12] Priya: Priya, platform eng, I'm the ops owner for the integration.
[00:15] Leah: Leah, CFO, i'll be quick today, mostly here for cost discussion.
[00:19] Samir: perfect. Jia, Ravi with me - short intros?
[00:22] Jia: hi team, Jia from CS, i'll be coordinating follow ups.
[00:25] Ravi: ravi se, focusing on perf and private deployment questions.
[00:29] Samir: great. quick agenda: numbers since last qtr, any reliability incidents, roadmap asks and next steps. anyone want to add?
[00:36] Carlos: no, that's good. we'll start with usage - we saw a 3x increase in embedding requests since December, and chat usage up about 40% mo-mo. costs are creeping.
[00:44] Leah: yes costs, please show any breakdown, we need visibility.
[00:48] Samir: sure, we pulled token-level billing and route-level breakdowns, i'll share the sheet after. high level - embedding units are now the majority of spend due to our nightly bulk vectorization jobs. Ravi, can you talk about batching and cache options?
[00:58] Ravi: yeah so two levers - batch size and prefix/KV cache. for embeddings batching helps throughput massively but may increase latency for small requests, we can recommend scheduled bulk windows and async job patterns. also prefix caching isn't used much for embeddings but for chat we can cache common system prompts.
[01:17] Priya: our problem is the nightly job spikes the cost, and we also need lower p95 latency for the support chat during peak hours. currently p95 is 1.8s at peak.
[01:26] Samir: 1.8s p95 - thanks. that's within hosted SLA but we can do better with Dedicated. dedicated pools let you pin capacity and reduce p95 to about mid-200ms p50 and <600ms p95 for the models you're running depending on instance types. caveat - commit costs.
[01:40] Leah: commit costs are my concern. can you show the math vs hosted? we run 24/7 workloads.
[01:46] Samir: absolutely. high level: for your current 3M embeddings/month + chat tokens, hosted cost is variable and last month spiked 28% due to the nightly jobs. Dedicated with reserved capacity plus burst can lower unit cost by ~30-40% depending on utilization. i'll send a detailed TCO later.
[02:02] Carlos: what about private deployment / VPC? we have data residency rules for some clients.
[02:07] Ravi: we support Private (VPC/on-prem) - that gives you control over network and KMS, audit logs. operational overhead is higher and there's a platform fee but it's common for regulated lines of business. we can do a hybrid where core inference is dedicated in Redwood-managed infra with a private control plane.
[02:22] Priya: what about the integration complexity - do we have to change our SDKs? we use our internal queuing layer.
[02:28] Samir: minimal changes. same API surface, but you can configure routing rules and pin routes to Dedicated pools. we'll provide onboarding templates and an infra playbook. Jia will own that.
[02:36] Jia: yes, we'll share the whiteglove onboarding checklist and a sample deployment diagram.
[02:40] Leah: security - we need SOC2 and ISO evidence, and SSO/SAML. any gaps?
[02:45] Ravi: Redwood's SOC2 Type II is available, ISO cert is documented; SSO via SAML/OIDC supported, RBAC and key management integrates with customer KMS/HSM. i'll attach the audit pack.
[02:56] Carlos: quick note - we saw a small KV cache miss issue on Feb 18 that caused a latency spike and a retry storm, can we review root cause?
[03:04] Ravi: yes i pulled logs - root cause was an eviction policy mismatch combined with our default batching window. some requests evicted mid-session leading to rewarm and retries. fix: tweak cache TTLs and bump batch window during rewarm periods. we'll propose config changes.
[03:19] Priya: will that require model changes?
[03:21] Ravi: no model changes, just runtime config and kernel selection tweaks. might need a short maintenance window for testing.
[03:28] Samir: good. next, roadmap and feature asks - Carlos wanted per-route cost attribution and alerts.
[03:33] Carlos: yes, we need per-feature cost alerts (thresholds) and a dashboard for token burn by endpoint.
[03:39] Samir: console supports token-level breakdown and custom alerts now, we can set per-route thresholds and integrate with PagerDuty or webhooks. i'll work with you on sensible defaults.
[03:48] Leah: on contracts - if we commit to Dedicated, what does the cancellation / ramp look like?
[03:52] Samir: typical reserved capacity contracts have a 12-month minimum with 60-day notice for scale changes, we can discuss a pilot/beta period to lower risk. pricing and contract cadence i'll send in the proposal.
[04:03] Carlos: about benchmarks - we'd like p50/p95, throughput at our seq lengths (avg 512 for chat + 2048 for embeddings), and memory/kv behavior.
[04:12] Ravi: we'll run a benchmark with your sample corpus. prefer to run it on a Dedicated mirror to show realistic numbers; if not possible we can simulate with hosted but results vary.
[04:22] Priya: we'll share the traffic profile and a sample request set.
[04:25] Samir: perfect. action items recap at the end.
[04:29] Jia: quick question from priy a, sorry - can we get a cost-savings estimate with quantization/8-bit models?
[04:35] Ravi: yes quantization helps significantly for embeddings and many decoder models, but quality tradeoffs depend on evals. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per workload; we'll run small evals.
[04:47] Leah: make sure finance gets the savings scenarios in writing.
[04:50] Samir: noted.
[04:52] Carlos: anything about competitors? our infra team looked at Anthropic and OpenAI for hosted, and Replicate for self-hosting - main reasons to look were quality for instruction-following and simpler integration.
[05:02] Samir: noted - we'll highlight where Redwood reduces ops lift vs self-host and shows unit cost comparisons vs hosted alternatives.
[05:10] Jia: ok, i'll list follow ups: share SOC2 + ISO pack, onboarding checklist, pricing proposal, schedule benchmark.
[05:16] Priya: thanks. can we aim to have the benchmark by next Friday?
[05:19] Ravi: yes i'll book a slot for 2026-03-12 and confirm with Carlos.
[05:23] Samir: quick recap of next steps: Samir sends pricing and TCO, Jia shares security and onboarding docs, Ravi runs benchmark, Carlos shares traffic profile. any other items?
[05:33] Leah: no, that's it from finance side.
[05:35] Carlos: thanks everyone, good meeting.
[05:37] Samir: thanks team - we'll follow up.

End of call.
